summary: Shared durable-consumer contract checks: distinguish durable deletion, validate envelope type against subject
description:
TKT-99's broker-level test asserts the exact waitConsume diagnostic, but that message covers every async termination ("durable deleted or subscription terminated"). The test therefore proves deletion happened and that something terminated the consume context — not that the first caused the second. jetstream distinguishes them (ErrConsumerDeleted, pull.go:722); access does not surface it. Fix is a production diagnostic/readiness-surface change, so it was split out of the test-only ticket.

---

## Absorbed TKT-133 — inventory never validates the envelope `type` against the subject

Inventory's catalog consumer dispatches purely on the NATS subject
(`knownSchemas[msg.Subject()]`, `services/inventory/internal/consumer/consumer.go:201`) and ignores
`type` entirely. Access checks it in both consumers (`consumer.go:360`, `policy.go:96`).
Pre-existing at `origin/main`; TKT-126 preserved the behaviour deliberately and recorded the
asymmetry in ADR-033 rather than silently fixing it.

ADR-009 §5 makes `type == subject` part of the envelope contract, so inventory currently accepts
envelopes that violate it. And TKT-126 introduced an inconsistency, deliberately and with a test
(`TestDecodeEnvelopeRejectsNonStringType`): a **non-string** `type` fails the shared decode and
terminates, while a **wrong-string** `type` is accepted — disposition depends on the JSON
representation of the same contract violation.

Sub-scope:
- [ ] Inventory validates `env.Type` against `msg.Subject()` before schema dispatch, **or** the
      decision not to is recorded with a reason (the broker, not the payload, may be the deliberate
      routing authority)
- [ ] Missing / mismatched / non-string `type` reach the **same** disposition class, not three
- [ ] Consumer-level tests pin the chosen behaviour for all three shapes, at a known and a future
      schema, asserting the exact action sequence and the readiness outcome
- [ ] ADR-033's "what deliberately does not live here" section and the `domainevent` package doc match

## Why these are one ticket

Both belong to `shared/go/durableconsumer` — TKT-133's own text says the `id`/`type` checks belong in
the skeleton, and TKT-127 (which built it) is now **Done**, so this is where they land. TKT-123's
diagnostic moved there too when TKT-127 lifted `waitConsume`
(`shared/go/durableconsumer/wait.go:83`), which means fixing it once now covers access *and*
inventory instead of only access as originally scoped.

Both halves are the same question asked at two layers: **what does this consumer actually verify
before it acts, and can it tell you which thing went wrong?** One plan gate.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Split out of TKT-99's ai-review as an incidental finding (R4, medium) — real, but its fix is a
production change that a test-only ticket had no business making.

**The finding.** TKT-99's smoke test proves durable deletion terminates the access consumer by
asserting the exact diagnostic access writes:

> `access: access-slot-policy: consume context closed (durable deleted or subscription terminated)`

That message is produced by `consumer.waitConsume` for *any* async termination. So the test proves
(a) we deleted the durable and (b) *something* terminated the consume context — not that (a) caused
(b). A coincident NATS connection or subscription failure inside the 15s window would satisfy both
counters even if durable deletion had stopped closing `ConsumeContext.Closed()` entirely. The
strongest form of the test is currently unreachable from outside the process.

**Why it is small in practice, and still worth closing.** The window is 15s, the smoke stack is a
single-node hermetic broker, and a broker failure would break the rest of the suite loudly. But the
test's whole value is causal, and it is one indistinguishable log line away from being decorative.

**Shape of the fix.** `waitConsume` receives only a closed channel, so it cannot name the cause.
`jetstream` exposes it: `ErrConsumerDeleted` is what `pull.go:722` treats as terminal. Surfacing
the terminal error — via the consume error handler, or by having the caller record the last
terminal error alongside the latch — would let both the log line and the test say *deleted*
specifically. That is a change to ADR-017's readiness/termination surface and to a diagnostic
operators read, so it wants its own plan and its own review.

**Also worth deciding in the same ticket:** whether the two `waitConsume` callers should report
distinguishable reasons at all, or whether "terminated, and here is the underlying error" is
enough. TKT-97 deliberately kept the message coarse; this is a revisit of that call, not a bug in it.

Code pointers: `services/access/internal/consumer/run.go` (`waitConsume`),
`services/access/internal/consumer/policy.go:212`, `consumer.go:429`,
`smoke/access_consumer_test.go` (`policyTermination`, the assertion that would tighten).
Governing ADR: ADR-017 §5b (§236-241).

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=readiness -->
### Gate 1 validation — re-verified against HEAD `ac2952b`

**Still real, path moved.** The undifferentiated diagnostic now lives in `shared/go/durableconsumer/wait.go:83` (lifted by TKT-127), not in access. No `ErrConsumerDeleted` reference anywhere in `services/`. Fixing it in the shared package now covers access and inventory at once — scope grew in the ticket's favour.

**Verdict: still worth doing → Ready.** Not DoR-baked: the 8-item shaping happens when the ticket is claimed, per the owner's drain-the-debt call.

### Merged TKT-133 into this ticket (backlog drain, 2026-07-29)

Was: *waitConsume's termination diagnostic can't distinguish durable deletion from any other subscription failure (TKT-99 ai-review R4)*

TKT-133 is now **Inventory never validates the envelope `type` against the subject (TKT-126 ai-review)** — absorbed above, and moved back to Backlog marked MERGED so it cannot be claimed twice. Its own thread stays readable on the board for the full filing history and review lineage.

Rationale: a plan gate + ai-review + PO gate on each half costs more than the work. See the *Why these are one ticket* section in the description.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claim — TKT-123

**Branch:** `TKT-123-consumer-contract-checks` off `origin/main` @ `468ee39`.

**Selection reason:** next in Ready by key. Zero open blockers — the only link is `absorbs TKT-133`,
parked in Backlog marked MERGED.

**Re-verified at claim time**, both halves still open:
- The diagnostic is still one string for every async termination
  (`shared/go/durableconsumer/wait.go`), and **neither service registers a
  `jetstream.ConsumeErrHandler`** — verified by `git grep`, it returns nothing. So the cause
  jetstream *does* distinguish (`ErrConsumerDeleted`, `pull.go:722`) is never captured.
- Inventory dispatches on `knownSchemas[msg.Subject()]` (`consumer.go:201`) and never reads
  `env.Type`; access checks it in both consumers.

**Direct interaction with TKT-122, which I merged twenty minutes ago.** That ticket rewrote this
exact function and its comments name this ticket: *"Changing the wording means changing both,
deliberately (and TKT-123, which wants a finer-grained cause, must do exactly that)."* Two
constraints carry forward and the plan must respect them:
1. The diagnostic string is a **contract**, asserted verbatim by `smoke/access_consumer_test.go`
   (TKT-99) *and* by `TestWaitTerminationDiagnosticIsExact`. Changing it means changing both.
2. `Wait` now returns **nil** when shutdown and closure are both observable — a deliberate,
   documented suppression. A finer-grained cause must not quietly reopen that.

**Risk: not `risk:low`.** Shared-kernel behaviour affecting two services, plus a disposition
decision on a contract violation.

### ⚠️ Gate waiver — this ticket ran GATELESS (process experiment)

Same waiver as TKT-116/117/119/122; the repo owner waived all four human gates for this run.
Gate 2 → agent self-resolves open decisions (prefer the critique's recommendation, else the most
reversible option), recorded in `kind=plan-final`. Gate 3 → agent merges after the ai-review
converges, review-guide posted first. Gate 4 → agent self-validates each COS against test evidence
on the merged code.

Unchanged: `config.models` routing with no substitution, cross-model review for plan and code, TDD
with tests observed red first, `make check` green before every push and after the merge, all marker
comments, no AI attribution.

**Model routing:** `plan` = `gpt-5.6-sol` · `planReview` = `main-agent` · `implement` = `main-agent`
· `aiReview` = `gpt-5.6-sol`.

**No CI:** no Actions minutes; `make check` is the sole gate; branch protection not enforced (403).
